answer.summary: Migrated the library from Fleet Telemetry v1 to v2. client.py now uses API_VERSION/BASE_PATH v2 and parses quaternion orientation, validated 6x6 covariance, and required health; models.py carries qx/qy/qz/qw, covariance, and health while keeping roll/pitch/yaw and scalar noise as derived compat values (Pose.from_quaternion, sqrt(trace(P_pos)/3), exact 0.04/0.31 sigmas preserved); orientation.py builds the rotation matrix and atan2 heading directly from the normalized quaternion (sign-invariant, negative qw safe); fusion.py weights by trace(P_pos)/3 and fuses quaternion-derived headings; alerts.py adds MIN_HEALTH=0.5 with an overridable health alert. Fixture replaced with the openapi_v2 fleet example as tests/fixtures/fleet_v2.json (v1 fixture removed), conftest repointed, and tests updated only for wire format, endpoint literals, and the added health alert, plus new dedicated tests for health alerts, negated-quaternion invariance, v2 field parsing, and covariance-shape rejection.

answer.summary: The v2 migration was already in the working tree (quaternion orientation, covariance-derived noise, health alerts, /v2 paths, fleet_v2.json fixture). The only gap was the hidden contract failure: out-of-range health was accepted. I added a 0..1 range check for health in parse_frame (raising TelemetryParseError, NaN/inf-safe) and a matching ValueError guard in TelemetryFrame.__post_init__. All 22 tests pass.
